articles.summary: Erling Haaland’s Manchester derby winner reignites the VAR debate
articles.body:
World Service , · 30 Sep 2026 , · 43 mins

Manchester City striker Erling Haaland’s controversial winner in the recent Manchester derby has reignited the debate over VAR in football. Should the video assistant referee be scrapped, or can it be improved? How does it work in other countries, and can football learn anything from other sports? Former Premier League VAR official Graham Scott and CBS Sports analyst Michael Lahoud - a former Sierra Leone and MLS striker - join the BBC's John Bennett to debate ten ways VAR could be improved. We also hear from the BBC’s football issues correspondent Dale Johnson, who explains how VAR works across Europe, as well as BBC rugby union correspondent Chris Jones, who explains how video technology works in rugby. Unexpected questions and beyond the scoresheet chat. More than the Score tells stories from all over the world of sport. From Formula One to netball, MMA to figure skating, and Grand Slam tennis to Diamond League athletics. We've got interviews with extraordinary athletes, as well as the experts working behind the scenes, from football super-agents to the coaches keeping athletes in peak form. Plus, we've got the expertise of the BBC's top journalists, who share their insights from decades of covering sport at all levels. articles.title: Texas Supreme Court reverses Houston resident’s Sharia law divorce in Pakistan
articles.summary: (The Center Square) – The Texas Supreme Court has intervened in a Houston divorce dispute ruling that a divorce granted through Islamic Sharia law in Pakista...
articles.body:
The Texas Supreme Court ruled that a divorce granted through Islamic Sharia law in Pakistan is not valid in Texas due to lack of notice and consent from the wife.

The case raises questions about visa and marriage fraud, arranged marriages, and the jurisdiction of Pakistani courts in the context of Islamic Sharia law.

Texas lawmakers, including Gov. Greg Abbott and Lt. Gov. Dan Patrick, have taken actions to combat Sharia law, with some launching anti-Sharia law caucuses and filing bills to ban its application in the state.

(The Center Square) – The Texas Supreme Court has intervened in a Houston divorce dispute ruling that a divorce granted through Islamic Sharia law in Pakistan is not valid in Texas.

The case raises questions about visa and marriage fraud, arranged marriages and Islamic Sharia law, which Republican state and federal lawmakers have rallied against.

The case involves Houston residents and Pakistani nationals Mohammad Ali Choudhri and Hira Azhar who were married in Pakistan through an arranged marriage and divorced in Pakistan through Sharia law, according to court documents. The Texas Supreme Court agreed to hear an appeal brought by Azhar in a Harris County case.

At issue is the Islamic Sharia Law practice of talaq and jurisdiction of Pakistani courts. According to court documents, Choudhri, Pakistani and Harris County courts acknowledge he used the Sharia law practice of talaq in 2013. This involves an Islamic husband divorcing his wife by stating he divorces her three times.

Choudhri divorced Azhar through talaq "without her knowledge or consent … His wife was not served with process. She was not heard. She received no notice at all until two years after the divorce was final," the Texas Supreme Court said in its ruling .

The Islamic Sharia Council in London explains that under Sharia law, the husband is supposed to first ask for an arbitration meeting. If reconciliation fails, "he may divorce her either verbally or in writing – known as Talaq," with two witnesses present and only "when his wife is not on her menses, and when there has been no sexual contact with her since the time of her last menses," it says. After he pronounces the divorce, "his wife must wait for a given period of 3 months or 3 menstrual cycles. During this period, the wife is allowed to stay in the same house and the husband is responsible for her welfare and maintenance."

Under U.S. law, the "principle of natural justice" applies, the Texas Supreme Court said. This "requires a person to have notice of a suit before he can be conclusively bound by its result."

"The Pakistani divorce judgment was issued contrary to these principles. Accordingly, it cannot be afforded comity. We reverse and remand to the trial court for further proceedings consistent with this opinion," the high court ruled.

According to court documents, in 2008, Choudhri traveled to Pakistan to marry Azhar in an arranged marriage when he was 28 and she was 18. She then came to Houston in 2010 after obtaining a visa.

Arranged marriages are recognized in the U.S., including in Texas. Because age and consent are questionable in arranged marriages, a movement to ban child marriage at the state level is ongoing. Depending on the circumstance, arranged marriages may violate federal immigration law and constitute visa fraud.

In 2012, Azhar returned to Pakistan to renew her visa. In 2013, Choudhri traveled to Pakistan to divorce her through talaq, according to court documents. In 2015, she challenged the divorce in Pakistan and in Harris County. In 2018, the Pakistan Supreme Court ruled against her, stating they were divorced through talaq in 2013.

The Harris County trial court next dismissed her divorce petition based on its ruling, granting comity. Comity refers to courts in "one state or jurisdiction respecting the laws and judicial decisions of other jurisdictions," including international. She then appealed.

Prior to both rulings, in 2017, the Texas legislature enacted HB 45 , which required the Texas Supreme Court to adopt rules and provide judicial instruction regarding the application of foreign laws in certain family law cases. In 2018, Rule 308b went into effect, which requires hearings to determine the enforceability of a judgment or arbitration award based on foreign law in certain lawsuits under Texas family code.

Although Azhar sued before Rule 308b took effect, the high court agreed to review her case.

Eleven years after Azhar filed for divorce in Texas, the Texas Supreme Court ruled, "Other countries are welcome to conclude otherwise, but their judgments are not entitled to comity in a Texas court. No foreign judgment is entitled to comity when it contradicts the fundamental guarantees of the Texas and United States Constitutions. For the reasons set out above, the Pakistani proceeding challenged here exemplifies the type of foreign judgment that Texas courts may not enforce."

It also cited an 1895 U.S. Supreme Court ruling that held that "no sovereign is ever required to recognize the judgment of a foreign sovereign, and comity 'is neither a matter of absolute obligation, on the one hand nor of mere courtesy and good will, upon the other.'"

The ruling comes after Texas leaders implemented a range of anti-Sharia law measures and the Trump administration prioritized identifying visa and marriage fraud , The Center Square reported.

Texas Republican congressmen Chip Roy and Keith Self launched a Sharia Free America Caucus and filed multiple bills as did Sen. John Cornyn, including the Defeat Sharia Law in America Act and the No Sharia Act.

Gov. Greg Abbott has also taken multiple actions to combat Sharia law, including launching an investigation into a Sharia tribunal in north Texas. Lt. Gov. Dan Patrick listed banning Sharia law in Texas as a top legislative priority . Texas House Republicans created a Sharia Free Caucus, and in March, 95% of Republican primary voters supported a measure to ban Sharia law in Texas.

articles.title: VÍDEO: aviões ficam danificados após vendaval destruir hangares de aeroclube no Paraná | G1
articles.standfirst: Aeronaves estavam guardadas nos hangares do Aeroclube de Toledo. Estruturas metálicas foram arrancadas pelo vento e lançadas sobre rodovia.
articles.summary: Aeronaves estavam guardadas nos hangares do Aeroporto Municipal Luiz Dalcanale Filho, em Toledo. Estruturas metálicas foram arrancadas pelo vento e lançadas sobre rodovia.
articles.body:
Fortes ventos afetaram Toledo , no Oeste do Paraná, na tarde de terça-feira (29). Um aeroclube foi atingido e aviões foram arrastados e virados de ponta cabeça com a força das rajadas.

Vídeos feitos após o temporal mostram aeronaves atingidas e estruturas metálicas retorcidas no Aeroclube de Toledo. Os aviões estavam guardados nos hangares quando as estruturas foram destruídas pela força do vento. Assista acima.

Até a última atualização desta reportagem, não havia confirmação de quantas aeronaves foram danificadas nem informações sobre o valor dos prejuízos.

A força do vento também arrancou partes das estruturas metálicas, que foram lançadas sobre a PR-182. Árvores e postes caíram na região.

A rodovia ficou totalmente interditada nos dois sentidos no km 329. Equipes trabalharam durante a noite para retirar os materiais que bloqueavam a pista. O trânsito foi liberado por volta de 0h30 desta quarta-feira (30). A região também registrou falta de energia.

articles.body:
Dezoito apostas registradas em Sergipe acertaram quatro dezenas do concurso 3.064 da Mega-Sena em sorteio realizado pela Caixa Econômica Federal, nesta terça-feira (29).

O prêmio para as apostas que acertassem as seis dezenas era de R$ 49,5 milhões . No entanto, ninguém levou a faixa principal e o valor acumulou para R$ 75 milhões .

Veja os números sorteados: 04 - 10 - 20 - 25 - 27 – 48.

Os valores distribuídos aos contemplados em Sergipe variam entre R$ 727,39 e R$ R$ 4.364,30 , dependendo da modalidade do bilhete.

Confira apostas ganhadoras da Mega-Sena 3064 em Sergipe

Aracaju : sete apostas simples e dois bolões;

Itaporanga D’Ajuda : uma aposta simples;

Nossa Senhora do Socorro : duas apostas simples e um bolão;

O g1 passou a transmitir, desde abril, todos os sorteios das Loterias Caixa, ao vivo . A transmissão começa momentos antes de cada dia de concursos, no site e no canal do g1 no YouTube.

A Mega tem três sorteios semanais: às terças, quintas e domingos .

Volantes da Mega-Sena — Foto: Rafa Neddermeyer / Agência Brasil

A aposta mínima custa R$ 6 e pode ser realizada também pela internet, até as 20h – saiba como fazer a sua aposta online . Para concorrer, é necessário ter mais que 18 anos de idade.

Os jogos podem ser realizados até as 20h (horário de Brasília) em qualquer lotérica do país ou por meio do site e aplicativo Loterias Caixa, disponíveis em smartphones, computadores e outros dispositivos.

Já os bolões digitais poderão ser comprados até as 20h30, exclusivamente pelo portal Loterias Online e pelo aplicativo.

O pagamento da aposta online pode ser realizado via PIX, cartão de crédito ou pelo internet banking, para correntistas da Caixa. É preciso ter 18 anos ou mais para participar.

A probabilidade de vencer em cada concurso varia de acordo com o número de dezenas jogadas e do tipo de aposta realizada. Para um jogo simples, com apenas seis dezenas, que custa R$ 6, a probabilidade de ganhar o prêmio milionário é de 1 em 50.063.860, segundo a Caixa.

Já para uma aposta com 20 dezenas (limite máximo), com o preço de R$ 232.560,00, a probabilidade de acertar o prêmio é de 1 em 1.292, ainda de acordo com a instituição.

articles.title: VÍDEO: enxurrada invade casa, estoura vidro e arrasta móveis durante temporal no Paraná | G1
articles.standfirst: Morador registrou o momento em que a água tomou os cômodos em São Miguel do Iguaçu. “Coisa de filme”, relata Rafael Miranda.
articles.summary: Morador registrou o momento em que a água tomou os cômodos em São Miguel do Iguaçu. “Coisa de filme”, relata Rafael Miranda.
articles.body:
Uma enxurrada invadiu a casa de Rafael Miranda, estourou uma porta de vidro e arrastou móveis durante o temporal que atingiu São Miguel do Iguaçu, no oeste do Paraná, na noite de terça-feira (29).

Vídeos feitos pelo morador mostram a água barrenta tomando os cômodos da residência. Em alguns pontos, a força da correnteza forma pequenas ondas dentro do imóvel. Assista acima.

Rafael contou que percebeu a água entrando pelas frestas e tentou abrir uma porta para permitir que ela escoasse. Antes que conseguisse, porém, a pressão da água começou a deformar o vidro.

“Quando eu vi, o vidro começou a entortar, envergar. Quando estourou, foi aquela manifestação de água enorme, aquele desespero”, contou.

Casa foi alagada por água da chuva — Foto: Rafael Miranda

Com a entrada da enxurrada, mesas e outros objetos foram arrastados. Segundo Rafael, uma cadeira foi encontrada na rua.

A água também chegou à altura da janela do quarto da filha do morador.

“É coisa que eu nunca tinha visto. Coisa de filme, parece. Foram dois, três minutos de desespero”, relatou.

Na cidade, cerca de 100 pessoas ficaram desalojadas. As famílias foram levadas para um ginásio, enquanto equipes trabalham no levantamento dos danos. Segundo as informações do município, os ventos chegaram a 62,6 km/h.

articles.title: 'Sangue por todo lado': relato de passageira de voo desviado de Israel | G1
articles.standfirst: Segunda a mãe de uma passageira que estava a bordo, a filha lhe contou que "havia sangue por toda parte", e que, após ela ouvir gritos, viu um homem pegar uma faca e jogar o piloto no chão.
articles.summary: Segunda a mãe de uma passageira que estava a bordo, a filha lhe contou que, após ela ouvir gritos, viu um homem pegar uma faca e jogar o piloto no chão.
articles.body:
Um homem tentou matar um dos piloto do voo com destino a Israel que foi desviado para a Arábia Saudita , nesta quarta-feira (30), após uma suposta briga, de acordo com relatos feitos à agência de notícias Reuters.

Segunda a mãe de uma passageira que estava a bordo, a filha lhe contou que "havia sangue por toda parte", e que, após ela ouvir gritos, viu um homem pegar uma faca e jogar o piloto no chão.

"Ela me ligou [após aterrissar] e disse que eles ouviram vozes, alguém pediu ajuda. Era o piloto. Ele estava gritando: ‘Ajuda, ajuda, ajuda!’. O avião começou a perder o controle, então todas as pessoas começaram a gritar e acharam que iriam morrer. Depois de alguns minutos, outros dois pilotos assumiram o controle. Alguns israelenses correram até um homem, e nesse momento ele pegou uma faca e tentou matar o piloto. Eles seguraram a mão dele e o colocaram no chão. Havia muito sangue por toda parte", relatou Yasmin Abu Kasis.

Ainda de acordo com Yasmin, os passageiros ficaram "estressados e em choque" com toda a situação.

Em um vídeo supostamente gravado por um passageiro israelense a bordo do voo da Flydubai e amplamente divulgado pela mídia israelense, o passageiro afirma que um dos pilotos ficou gravemente ferido após ser esfaqueado e o outro sofreu ferimentos leves.

Dois oficiais israelenses afirmam que o copiloto teria esfaqueado o comandante antes que a tripulação de cabine entrasse na cabine de comando e assumisse o controle da aeronave.

O voo FZ1073 da companhia Flydubai saiu de Dubai , nos Emirados Árabes Unidos, e tinha como destino Tel Aviv . O avião sobrevoava a Jordânia quando desviou sua rota rumo à Arábia Saudita após emitir sinais de emergência em três ocasiões distintas.

Em uma delas, a aeronave chegou a transmitir o código de sequestro, segundo o site de monitoramento aéreo Flightradar24.

O voo aterrissou em território saudita por volta das 4h30 no horário de Brasília e todos os passageiros estavam seguros, anunciou a Flydubai.

O aeroporto de Tabuk, na Arábia Saudita, afirmou que tanto o piloto quanto o copiloto ficaram feridos e foram hospitalizados.

Os dados de voo indicaram que a aeronave desceu de forma repentina e rápida e desceu cerca de 14 mil pés em menos de 30 segundos pouco antes do primeiro sinal de emergência ser emitido, informou o Flightradar24.

Voo FZ1073 da Flydubai com destino a Tel Aviv desvia rota após incidente a bordo em 30 de setembro de 2026. — Foto: Flightradar24.com/Handout via REUTERS

O incidente provocou uma grande operação de segurança em Israel, que não mantém relações diplomáticas oficiais com a Arábia Saudita, onde o avião pousou. Netanyahu realizou consultas sobre o caso e seu gabinete afirmou que todos os esforços estavam sendo feitos para levar os passageiros israelenses de volta a Israel.

A mídia israelense afirmou que o Mossad, a principal agência de inteligência do país e responsável por operações especiais e secretas, está investigando o incidente.

Havia ao menos 150 passageiros israelenses a bordo, segundo a mídia de Israel. A Flydubai opera voos diários entre Dubai e Tel Aviv, uma rota popular entre cidadãos israelenses.

articles.title: Vendaval causa destelhamentos, queda de árvores e deixa famílias desalojadas em Monte Sião | G1
articles.standfirst: Segundo a Defesa Civil, os ventos chegaram a 110 km/h. Foram registrados 12,5 milímetros de chuva.
articles.summary: Segundo a Defesa Civil, os ventos chegaram a 110 km/h. Foram registrados 12,5 milímetros de chuva.
articles.body:
A chuva, acompanhada por um vendaval, causou diversos estragos em Monte Sião (MG), no fim da tarde de terça-feira (29). O temporal durou cerca de dez minutos e causou destelhamentos e queda de árvores. Não houve feridos, mas duas famílias ficaram desalojadas.

Segundo a Defesa Civil, os ventos chegaram a 110 km/h. Foram registrados 12,5 milímetros de chuva.

Vendaval arranca estrutura de quadra e causa danos à creche em Monte Sião — Foto: Defesa Civil/Divulgação

A região central foi uma das mais atingidas. A estrutura do telhado da quadra da Escola Municipal Professora Denise Maria Francisco Corsi foi arrancada pela força do vento e atingiu a creche Trem da Alegria, que fica em uma rua paralela.

Por causa dos danos, as aulas estão suspensas nas duas instituições até segunda-feira.

Vendaval causa estragos em Monte Sião, MG — Foto: Defesa Civil/Divulgação

O temporal também provocou danos em veículos, destruição de estruturas metálicas, destelhamento de imóveis, queda de árvores.

Houve rompimento da fiação, o que causou interrupções no fornecimento de energia elétrica, internet e telefonia. Cerca de 2 mil moradores foram afetados. No início da manhã desta quarta-feira (30), cerca de 300 unidades ainda estavam sem energia.

Vendaval causou destelhamentos e queda de árvores em Monte Sião, MG — Foto: Defesa Civil/Divulgação

articles.title: Estudante impedido de fazer vestibular da UFG por bomba de insulina se | G1
articles.standfirst: João Pedro Ladislau tem diabetes desde a infância e utiliza bomba de insulina. O Instituto Verbena informou que o candidato não formalizou o pedido no prazo previsto no edital para o uso de dispositivos médicos.
articles.summary: João Pedro, de 17 anos, disse que se sentiu acuado após ser impedido de fazer o vestibular da UFG por usar bomba de insulina.
articles.body:
O estudante João Pedro Ladislau, de 17 anos, impedido de realizar a prova do vestibular da Universidade Federal de Goiás (UFG) por ausa do uso do Sistema de Infusão Contínua de Insulina, contou que se sentiu acuado e desamparado diante da situação. Em entrevista ao g1 , o candidato, que convive com o diabetes desde a infância e depende do aparelho, relatou que não conseguiu anexar o laudo médico no momento da inscrição.

“Durante o momento lá, eu me senti bastante acuado, triste, principalmente por ser uma prova tão importante para mim, que eu teria expectativa de passar”, desabafou o jovem.

A prova aconteceu no domingo (27) e, antes do início da aplicação do exame, o estudante procurou a coordenação no local para informar que precisava usar a bomba de insulina. Mesmo tentando argumentar, o jovem disse que foi informado de que não poderia fazer a prova e acabou retirado do local.

O impacto emocional inicial, segundo João Pedro, só começou a diminuir após o apoio recebido com a repercussão do caso.

“Mas agora, com toda essa repercussão que está acontecendo, me sinto mais tranquilo. Muita gente já passou pela mesma coisa que eu e, cada vez mais o pessoal comentando, eu fico mais tranquilo”, disse.

Ao g1 , o Instituto Verbena informou que, para o uso de dispositivos médicos como a bomba de insulina, é necessário comunicar com antecedência a comissão organizadora por e-mail, pelo menos três dias antes da prova. De acordo com o instituto, “o candidato não formalizou a solicitação com a documentação exigida dentro do prazo previsto no edital” (leia a nota completa abaixo) .

João Pedro Ladislau contou que foi impedido de fazer vestibular da UFG por causa da bomba de insulina — Foto: Arquivo Pessoal/Alana Ladislau

Segundo a servidora Alana Ladislau, de 36 anos, mãe de João Pedro, o laudo médico comprovando a necessidade não havia sido anexado no momento da inscrição por um erro no sistema. Segundo ela, a inscrição, no valor de R$ 130, foi finalizada sem o documento.

Ao g1 , Alana explicou que não registrou o erro por não imaginar que teria todo esse transtorno.

“Foi bobeira nossa não registrar esse erro, não imaginávamos que fosse gerar todo esse transtorno e não queríamos que tivesse acontecido. Quando eles pediram o erro respondendo ao e-mail que eu havia enviado, eu já havia feito e pago a inscrição”, disse.

De acordo com Alana, ela e o filho tentaram fazer a inclusão do laudo por e-mail, já que não haviam conseguido anexá-lo no momento da inscrição, mas receberam como opção apenas a realização de uma nova inscrição.

“No e-mail eles responderam que teria que pagar novamente a inscrição. Eles disseram que teria que informar até três dias antes da prova, porém tentamos contato dois meses antes”, completou.

Segundo a mãe de João Pedro, o filho ficou muito ansioso porque tinha a expectativa de fazer uma prova que aguardava há muito tempo.

“Graças a Deus que agora tem a chance do Enem.”

Alana falou sobre a frustração com a situação do filho e explicou as limitações enfrentadas por pessoas com diabetes, especialmente crianças. Segundo ela, João Pedro convive com a doença desde o primeiro ano de vida.

“Muita coisa ele não lembra, mas teve o processo de negação dele na infância, vergonha de todos, tentando esconder e não querendo nem medir a glicemia na frente de ninguém... A bomba de insulina, além de ajudar no controle da glicemia, traz mais qualidade de vida para o diabético. Sem dúvidas, hoje é o melhor tratamento e, para eles que têm desde bebê, evita futuros problemas de saúde”, explicou.

Alana e o filho João Pedro, impedido de realizar prova de vestibular — Foto: Arquivo Pessoal/Alana Ladislau

‘Ele saiu da prova achando que era culpado’

A mãe do estudante, Alana, afirmou que a situação serviu como um aprendizado doloroso para o filho, que precisa lidar diariamente com o preconceito e a falta de informação.

“Infelizmente, não será a última vez que ele passará por isso. Por incrível que pareça, ele saiu da prova achando que era culpado, que estava cometendo um ‘crime’. Eu mostrei para ele que ele não pode se sentir assim, que a vida não dá moleza para ninguém, principalmente para quem tem diabetes. Ele tem que enfrentar as adversidades e saber dos seus direitos, pois esse aparelho salva a vida dele todos os dias e não é um crime usá-lo.”

Sem expectativa de que a banca organizadora ofereça uma solução ou reaplique a prova, João Pedro tenta superar o episódio concentrando as atenções no Exame Nacional do Ensino Médio (Enem):

“Eu não estou com nenhuma expectativa de fazer outra prova da UFG, [de] o Instituto Verbena elaborar uma nova prova para eu fazer, sei lá, mais alguns participantes. Eu estou com zero expectativa com isso. E agora a minha expectativa é o Enem, que é agora no final do ano. [Espero] que não aconteça o que aconteceu com a UFG e vai dar tudo certo.”

"O Instituto Verbena/UFG esclarece que, antes da aplicação das provas, o candidato recebeu orientação sobre os procedimentos necessários para solicitar a condição especial para uso de bomba de insulina, inclusive quanto à indicação dessa necessidade no sistema e ao envio do laudo médico.

O Instituto esclarece que a solicitação de condição especial não estava condicionada ao pagamento de nova taxa de inscrição.

Diante da informação de que havia dificuldade para anexar o laudo médico, o Instituto solicitou o envio de uma captura de tela da mensagem de erro ou da tela apresentada, para que pudesse verificar a situação e adotar as providências necessárias. Esse registro não foi encaminhado ao Instituto e não foi identificada falha no sistema que impedisse o envio da documentação.

O Edital nº 16/2026, em seu item 5.12.1, estabelece que o candidato que utiliza bomba de insulina deve comunicar previamente a situação à Comissão Organizadora, pelo e-mail indicado no edital, e apresentar a documentação exigida, no prazo de até 3 (três) dias úteis antes da prova.

Embora tenha recebido orientação antes da aplicação, o candidato não formalizou a solicitação com a documentação exigida dentro do prazo previsto no edital. A situação foi apresentada novamente à coordenação somente no dia da prova, quando já não era possível realizar a análise prévia e adotar os procedimentos necessários.

Quanto à reaplicação da prova, o edital (Item 5.8) não prevê nova oportunidade para situações decorrentes da ausência de solicitação prévia da condição especial ou do descumprimento dos procedimentos e prazos estabelecidos.

O Instituto Verbena/UFG reafirma que prestou as orientações cabíveis antes da prova e que o cumprimento das regras previstas no edital busca garantir isonomia entre os candidatos, segurança e regularidade do processo seletivo.

articles.title: Trump calls Kim Jong Un a ‘friend’ and plays down N Korea’s nuclear arsenal
articles.summary: US president’s comments came after he was asked why North Korea can have nuclear weapons when Iran cannot.
articles.body:
United States President Donald Trump has described North Korean leader Kim Jong Un as “a friend” and played down concerns about Pyongyang’s nuclear arsenal, saying, “as long as I’m around, he’s going to be fine”.

Trump made the remarks in Washington, DC, on Tuesday after a reporter asked him why North Korea could have nuclear weapons but Iran could not.

“That’s interesting. You know why? Because you had a different president, and they could have stopped him,” he said, referring to previous US administrations.

“He happens to be a friend of mine, Kim Jong Un, he’s a friend of mine. He likes Trump, doesn’t like a lot of other people. I’m about the only person in the entire world that he likes, and I like him,” he said.

He said North Korea’s nuclear capacity was “pretty large” but “not like us”.

“You know what, as long as I’m around, he’s going to be fine,” he added. “You know why? Because he respects me and he likes me.”

South Korea’s Defence Minister Ahn Gyu-back said last week that its northern neighbour possessed between 80 and 120 nuclear warheads. The figure is significantly higher than Trump’s recent assertion that Pyongyang has 57 nuclear weapons.

Trump is seeking to re-engage with Kim and secure a win on the international stage as the US and Israel’s war on Iran enters its eighth month.

The US president launched the war along with Israel on February 28, saying Iran could not have a nuclear weapon. Iran has denied seeking a weapon, noting it had signed an agreement with world powers in 2015 that curbed its nuclear programme in exchange for sanctions relief. But Trump abandoned the agreement during his first term in 2018.

The US-Israel war on Iran has disrupted global energy supplies, raised fuel costs and hurt Trump’s popularity ahead of the November midterm elections.

Trump held summits with North Korea’s Kim in 2018 and 2019, but diplomacy broke down over US demands that Pyongyang give up its nuclear weapons. Since then, Kim has expanded his arsenal of nuclear-capable missiles and strengthened his diplomatic footprint by aligning with Russia over its war in Ukraine and tightening relations with China.

Trump had earlier said he planned to hold in-person talks with Kim before the end of the year.

But North Korea has not formally committed to such a meeting.

articles.title: Gentle giant Backpack wins Alaska’s Fat Bear Week
articles.summary: The contest celebrates the resilience of the 2,200 brown bears that live in the preserve on the Alaska Peninsula.
articles.body:
After a week of fierce competition, Backpack emerged victorious as Fat Bear Week champion, the heftiest bear in Alaska’s Katmai National Park and Preserve.

The nonprofit running the longstanding contest announced on Tuesday that the bear, known for his pacifist nature, was the winner with more than 100,000 votes, giving him a close win over Bear 910 with just over 50 percent of the poll.

The contest, which is in its 12th year, celebrates the resilience of the 2,200 brown bears that live in the preserve on the Alaska Peninsula, which extends from the state’s southwest corner towards the Aleutian Islands. Fat Bear Week was started in 2014 as an interactive way to inform the public about brown bears, the coastal cousins of grizzlies.

Last year’s winner, Chunk — known officially as Bear 32 — clinched his victory at an estimated 1,200 pounds. He was handily defeated in the first round of competition this year by Bucky, who went on to lose a face-off against Backpack, known officially as Bear 89.

The event this year featured 16 bears vying for the heavyweight title in a single-elimination, bracket-style tournament. All voting is done online, and the winner was declared on Tuesday evening after the final poll closed. The public could watch the bears on explore.org’s livestream cameras before deciding on their favourite.

“Fat bears are successful bears,” the nonprofit says on its website. These bears gorge themselves on the abundant salmon that return to the Brooks River starting in late June. It is there that they can stuff themselves to accumulate the fat reserves they will need to survive the winter. To be featured in the contest, the bears must frequent the area around the river.

Backpack is the son of former Fat Bear Week champion Holly, who introduced him to the Brooks River when he was a first-year cub in 2006. His name was inspired by his habit of climbing onto his mother’s back when they swam the river. This year’s fans cheered on Backpack in the contest’s Instagram comments, noting his lineage and reputation as a gentle giant.

“Unlike many large adult male bears, Backpack hasn’t shown much aggression toward his competitors,” his contestant profile reads.

Backpack uses his “quiet strength” rather than brawling and is often seen in wildlife cameras sitting on a rock downstream, appearing to take in the scenery around him.

He defeated Bear 910, who is also the daughter of a former champion: 409 Beadnose.

Adult male brown bears typically weigh between 600 and 900 pounds (270-410kg) in midsummer. By the time they are ready to hibernate after feasting on migrating and spawning salmon, large males can weigh more than 1,000 pounds (454kg). Females are about one-third smaller. Bears may each eat as many as 30 fish a day this time of year, working hard to eat a year’s worth of food in about six months.

During winter hibernation, bears do not eat or drink and can lose one-third of their body weight.

Fat Bear Week’s contestants also included five bear families, in recognition of the record-high number of families and cubs at the river this summer. A mother must feed and protect her cubs while also eating enough calories to sustain herself through hibernation. Cubs often face the risk of attack from other bears due to territorialism or food scarcity.

Bear 132 and her three spring cubs advanced to the semifinals, but lost out to Bear 910.

She has become one of the largest and most experienced mother bears at Brooks River, according to her contestant profile. In mid-July, one of her cubs became separated from the family for several days, wandering the river corridor alone. The cub was reunited with the family a few days later.

articles.title: Manchester Airport reviews parking following traffic complaints
articles.summary: Taxi drivers complain about standing traffic on roads around Terminal 2, leading to delayed pick-ups.
articles.body:
Parking arrangements at Manchester Airport are being reviewed after several taxi firms reported significant road traffic congestion in recent months.

They have complained about standing traffic on routes around Terminal 2, leading to significant delays in picking up passengers.

Abu Bakar, from MCR Elite Transfers, said: "It's very frustrating for me because I am wasting time in traffic and it takes its toll on you because it makes you tired."

Manchester Airport said it was carrying out an "extensive review" and referred to "a range of factors including lower passenger-to-vehicle ratios caused by greater numbers of couples and solo travellers arriving in cars compared to the summer months".

Bakar added: "All of the time I am stuck in traffic means I'm losing money and my earnings are going to drop because of the congestion at the airport.

"It's been a problem for months and some of my passengers have had to wait for up to 30 minutes."

Other taxi firms have complained on social media about long queues on roads near Terminal 2.

A spokesperson for the airport added: "We are carrying out an extensive review of the system to identify ways of mitigating these issues.

"In the short term we have deployed extra traffic marshals to help keep things moving and we are working with Transport for Greater Manchester to change the timing of traffic lights in the area."

Manchester Airport has undergone a £1.3bn transformation in recent years, with the expansion earlier this year of Terminal 2 and the closure of Terminal 1.

Ryanair now operates exclusively from Terminal 3.

More than 32.4m passengers used Manchester Airport in the 12 months to the end of August 2026, representing an annual increase of 2%.

articles.title: Flydubai flight to Israel diverted to Saudi Arabia after emergency alert
articles.summary: Airline says plane experiences an ‘incident’ en route from Dubai to Tel Aviv, lands safely at Tabuk airport in Saudi Arabia.
articles.body:
A commercial flight from Dubai in the United Arab Emirates to Israel has been forced to make an emergency landing in Saudi Arabia.

The Flydubai plane transmitted an emergency alert shortly after takeoff on Wednesday, according to publicly available flight-tracking information.

The airline said the plane “experienced an incident while en route”, adding that it landed safely at Saudi Arabia’s Tabuk airport, which also happens to be a military base, and all passengers were safe and accounted for.

Flight-tracking data indicated that it was a Boeing 737 Max 8 aircraft.

According to data from the Flightradar24 website, the aircraft suddenly lost altitude during the flight, dropping from nearly 34,000 feet (more than 10km) at 05:21 GMT to less than 17,000 feet at 05:22 GMT.

The plane issued an “unlawful interference” alert, apparently due to an altercation between the pilots on board, Israeli media reports said, citing officials.

The pilot and copilot were admitted to hospital with injuries, Tabuk airport said, adding that it was coordinating with Flydubai to secure a replacement aircraft.

Israel said it was organising the safe return of Israeli passengers from Saudi Arabia.

“The incident is under control, and all measures are currently being deployed in order to return the Israeli passengers safely to Israel,” a statement from Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s office said.

Passengers on the plane told Israel’s Channel 12 by phone that they heard shouts from the front of the plane and heard the altercation between the pilots, and that the plane dipped steeply before the emergency landing.

At the time of reporting, all the passengers were on the plane and there was a heavy presence of Saudi security forces around.

Yasmin Abukasis was quoted by the Reuters news agency as saying her daughter Miriam, who was among the passengers on the flight, had told her that she had heard screaming and that a man holding a knife had forced one of the pilots onto the floor, and that there was blood everywhere.

“What we understand, according to flight radar tracking, is that two emergency signals were transmitted from the flight – the first was a general emergency signal and the second, a few minutes later, seemed to indicate some kind of unlawful interference on the flight,” Al Jazeera’s Zein Basravi, reporting from Doha, Qatar, said.

“Tracking data also shows that the aircraft plunged nearly 14,000 feet within 30 seconds during the incident – a steep, sharp descent that would have unnerved passengers.”

Later on Wednesday, Flightradar24 temporarily showed a second Flydubai flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv diverting back to Dubai, but then showed it continuing on its planned route to Israel.

Flydubai is a low-cost sister carrier of Emirates airline. The UAE has become a popular holiday destination for Israeli tourists since the countries normalised ties in 2020.

Flydubai’s fleet relies entirely on variants of the 737, a twin-engine, single-aisle aircraft widely used by airlines around the world. It has nearly 100 planes, including 69 of the Max 8 variant.

The flight originated from Dubai airport, the Middle East’s busiest and the world’s largest in terms of international travel. It handled a record 95.2 million passengers last year.

It is not the first time a flight between Israel and the UAE has landed in Saudi Arabia. A Flydubai flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv made an emergency landing in Riyadh in September 2025 due to a medical incident, the Israeli media reported at the time.

articles.title: S Korea demands apology over DMZ blasts as N Korea denies planting mines
articles.summary: South Korea calls for a formal apology from North Korea over the DMZ explosion that injured three soldiers.
articles.body:
South Korea’s military has demanded an apology from North Korea over landmine explosions earlier this month in the border zone between the two countries that wounded three soldiers.

Three South Korean soldiers were injured in two explosions on September 21 near the military demarcation line in the western section of the Demilitarized Zone, a heavily fortified border buffer zone between the Koreas that is commonly known as the DMZ.

Kang Hyunwoo, the South Korean joint chiefs of staff’s director of operations, said the military “strongly urges” North Korea to apologise for the blasts and take “responsible measures” to prevent a recurrence.

“This is a clear violation of the Armistice Agreement and undermines the spirit of existing inter-Korean agreements; it must be stopped immediately,” he said on Wednesday, adding “we strongly urge an apology and responsible measures”.

Defence Minister Kang Shin-chul said South Korea would consider unspecified “corresponding measures” if a complete investigation confirms the North was responsible.

Kim Yo Jong, the sister of North Korean leader Kim Jong Un, said the South Korean assessment is a “conspiratorial farce” and accused Seoul of making groundless claims to create a pretext for provocation against Pyongyang.

She also criticised the South for broadcasting warnings and firing warning shots at North Korean troops conducting front-line fortification work, adding “our soldiers have never crossed the border”.

“If the [South Korean] military gangsters fire at our soldiers carrying on the permanent project for the southern border, not warning shots, our border units will take immediate and merciless retaliatory action,” she said.

The United Nations Command said on Wednesday it had “identified an active Democratic People’s Republic of Korea (North Korea’s) anti-personnel mine on the ROK side of the Military Demarcation Line”, in a joint investigation with Seoul’s military.

“Based on the findings of the investigation, UNC determined that an Armistice Agreement violation occurred,” it added.

The UN Command is a US-led multinational military force charged with overseeing the armistice agreement that halted fighting in the Korean War and administers the southern side of the DMZ.

articles.title: A TV journalist is crowned king of a traditional monarchy in Uganda
articles.summary: A journalist was crowned king of a traditional monarchy in Uganda after it lost its onetime “boy king” last month.
articles.body: KAMPALA, Uganda — A journalist was crowned king of a traditional monarchy on Tuesday after it lost its onetime “boy king” last month, triggering widespread grief and a succession dispute in Uganda’s Tooro Kingdom. The journalist is a prince who had long been employed as a broadcaster and editor with Uganda Broadcasting Corp. He picked the regnal name of Edward Rukidi Nyabongo. He performed rituals overnight, was ushered into the palace and was formally unveiled to his followers on Tuesday. Traditional kingdoms were banned in the 1960s, after Uganda’s independence from British colonial rule, by a republican president who said that he wanted to unify the country. They were restored in 1993. The coronation ceremony in Fort Portal, a remote town in western Uganda and not far from the Congo border, was watched by thousands in person and on televised broadcasts. Speaking at the event, Ugandan President Yoweri Museveni urged traditional leaders to promote local languages. In a brief speech at his coronation, Nyabongo pledged to be a unifying figure for all his people. Before his enthronement, the monarch told the local New Vision newspaper that “heritage must be matched by discipline and hard work. My family never let me treat royal descent as an entitlement; it was presented to me as a duty to prepare for.” Nyabongo wasn’t particularly high in the line of succession, but elders within the kingdom’s ruling clan, known as the Babiito, selected him from a pool of eligible princes after King Oyo Nyimba’s death from cancer at age 34 in August without a publicly known heir. The queen mother, Best Kemigisa, disputed that decision and charged that the written will of King Oyo hadn’t been followed in the selection of Nyabongo. Kemigisa said that Oyo left behind a young son whose identity would be unveiled at the right time, casting doubt on the legitimacy of Nyabongo and the decision of the Babiito to choose him. Local media cited scenes of disagreement — including a brief squabble over custody of the king’s remains — at Oyo’s Sept. 12 funeral. Although Oyo’s alleged son has yet to be revealed, purported photos of a “Baby Oyo” have flooded social media, giving hope to devotees of the deceased monarch. But critics say that the child, if he exists, should have been introduced to the kingdom’s elders while his father was still alive. “They have demonstrated that these are the norms of the kingdom,” Nicholas Sengoba, a prominent political analyst in Uganda, said of the Babiito’s selection of Nyabongo. “Many of these positions may not be popular.” Oyo was crowned in 1995, at the age of 3, after his father’s death. He was a curious child in colorful robes and an object of adoration for his hundreds of thousands of followers. At his coronation, he went through a series of tribal rituals and was led into the royal cemetery to perform a coming-of-age ceremony: successfully tossing nine coffee beans into his father’s tomb. Oyo once held the unofficial title of the world’s youngest king, a mesmerizing figure even for world leaders introduced to him at national events, including South Africa’s Nelson Mandela. Libyan leader Moammar Gadhafi was one of those who befriended the Tooro royal family as if they were part of his extended family. Gadhafi made multiple trips to Uganda and supported Oyo and Kemigisa for years before Gadhafi’s death in October 2011. Oyo was guided by regents appointed by the kingdom until he became an adult at 18.

articles.title: 90% of dementia cases in TN go undiagnosed: State turns focus to early screening and care
articles.summary: CHENNAI: With more than five lakh people in Tamil Nadu living with dementia, and 90% believed to be undiagnosed, the state is looking at making the
articles.body: CHENNAI: With more than five lakh people in Tamil Nadu living with dementia, and 90% believed to be undiagnosed, the state is looking at making the condition a “public health priority”.“Tamil Nadu has a rapidly ageing population. People over 60 make up 16% of the population in 2026, and it is projected to reach 20% in 10 years. The number of people with dementia is projected to double to 10 lakh,” says Ramani Sundaram of Dementia India Alliance (DIA), which recently organised DemCon in Chennai, a conference on the condition.DIA is a national organisation focused on dementia awareness, care, support and brain healthAt DemCon, state health minister K G Arunraj said the govt would work towards a “coordinated state plan”. “The MoU between the department of health and family welfare and DIA is an important step in this direction,” said Arun Raj. “This partnership is an expression of our shared commitment to strengthening dementia care.”The state plan will look at standardising screening, assessment, referral and treatment, as well as making diagnosis, systematic referrals and follow-up part of the existing primary healthcare infrastructure. “It’s important to create awareness as dementia care costs about Rs 3 lakh per person annually, apart from the informal cost of care provided by family members,” says Ramani. “Cognitive impairment cannot be reduced to simply asking an elderly person whether they are becoming forgetful.”An ongoing screening programme conducted since Feb by DIA in collaboration with the state govt among 2,500 elderly people in Coimbatore, Erode and Chengalpet, found 9% had cognitive impairment.Among those screened, 30% reported neurological problems such as slowness, tremors, falls or limb weakness, while 28% had sleep disturbances. About 27% reported feeling sad, irritable, or disinterested in their usual activities, while 18% had trouble with memory, wayfinding or planning. About 12% had difficulty speaking, understanding, naming, reading or writing, and 7% said they heard voices or saw images when alone.About 35% of those screened had hypertension, which, says Ramani, is among the risk factors for dementia. “There was substance abuse in about 15% of those screened, while a large percentage – 42 – chewed tobacco. These are also among the risk factors. Up to 45% of dementia can be prevented if these are addressed. articles.title: Cornell University gang-rape case: DA reveals new disturbing details as investigation reopens
articles.summary: The district attorney (DA) who has reopened his investigation into an alleged 2024 sexual assault at Cornell University has defended his earlier decision
articles.body: The district attorney (DA) who has reopened his investigation into an alleged 2024 sexual assault at Cornell University has defended his earlier decision not to prosecute anyone, citing the former student’s own account of the incident to police.Also Read | Drugged with ketamine, raped for hours: Ex-student sues Cornell University, 7 fraternity membersIn several media interviews on Tuesday (local time), Tompkins County DA Matthew Van Houten argued that while the male students involved did things that were “morally wrong”, the woman’s initial account of the incident to police did not include allegations that she was drugged, incapacitated beyond the ability to consent, or forced to engage in sexual activity.“She went to the police because she knew it wasn’t right,” Van Houten told CNN.“There were no question marks. There was no additional need to find information because we had all of the information that the police collected from Jane Doe through her very detailed, very comprehensive statement that she provided,” he added.Van Houten has not released the complainant’s sworn statement to police, but instead made public a summary that includes some of her direct quotes. He also defended his office’s decision not to conduct further investigation after the woman, identified in court filings by the pseudonym "Jane Doe," initially spoke to police.The woman filed a lawsuit this month alleging that she was assaulted by seven male students at the Chi Phi fraternity house on Cornell’s campus in October 2024. According to the lawsuit, the alleged incident occurred after she was pressured into taking drugs and consuming alcohol, leaving her unable to consent to sexual activity.The complainant reported the incident to Cornell’s campus police, but Van Houten’s office decided not to prosecute anyone at the time. The office later reopened the criminal investigation amid growing public attention over the woman’s allegations.Cornell supports reopening investigationCornell University has expressed support for reopening the criminal investigation, saying in a statement that its own inquiry had resulted in disciplinary action against some students, including expulsions.According to the statement, the Chi Phi chapter remains barred from campus.The woman’s lawsuit accuses the university of failing to prevent the alleged assaults and of not adequately addressing sexual violence on campus. It includes a photograph that purportedly shows a group chat between fraternity members discussing the events of that night.Van Houten dismissed the photograph as a “red herring”, arguing that it had no bearing on the legal assessment of whether the woman had consented or whether there was evidence that she had been unable to consent under state law.“We received it, but it was not relevant to the assessment of whether Jane Doe consented or whether there was any evidence of lack of consent on her part as defined by the penal law,” he said.(With AP inputs)You use AI every day. articles.title: Hurricane Polo’s remnants bringing more rain to flood-struck U.S. Southwest
articles.summary: As former Hurricane Polo weakened over northwestern Mexico on Tuesday evening, the storm’s remnants battered the U.S. Southwest
articles.body: PHOENIX — As former Hurricane Polo weakened over northwestern Mexico on Tuesday evening, the storm’s remnants battered the U.S. Southwest, flooding roadways and forcing residents in small New Mexico towns to evacuate over concerns about a dam failing. Polo had struck the Mexican state of Baja California Sur in the morning with maximum sustained winds of 110 mph (177 kph). It crossed the Gulf of California and weakened to become a tropical storm as it moved inland to the northeast. By Tuesday evening, the New Mexico Department of Transportation reported flooded roads and debris on highways across the state, while parts of Arizona had become especially drenched, leading to several water rescues. That is after storms rolled through parts of the U.S. Southwest overnight Monday, saturating the ground, which can make flooding worse. Later in the week, the flood risk is expected to move into parts of the central U.S., according to the National Weather Service. Southwest U.S. sees heavy rains and floods Bands of rain continued to sweep across the U.S. Southwest, causing desert rivers to surge and usually dry arroyos to rage with floodwater. The potential failure of the dam in south central New Mexico prompted evacuations in three small communities with hundreds of residents along the Rio Grande. People in Rincon, Salem and Garfield were told to seek higher ground immediately “before conditions worsen.” Residents were later told to evacuate from nearby Hatch, home to prized green chile crops, and farther north in Placitas. Wide swaths of the U.S. Southwest were under flood watches as the complex system of tropical weather spread northeast from Mexico, with Polo as the main event. “Definitely looking at the chances for urban flooding,” weather service meteorologist Carter Greulich in Albuquerque said. “Don’t drive through flooded roadways. Remain out of the arroyos, especially in our urban areas.” A person stranded on top of a vehicle in floodwaters west of Phoenix was rescued Tuesday morning. Video taken by Arizona Fire and Medical Services showed a helicopter lowering a rescuer to a person clinging to their overturned car. And in Zion National Park, in Utah, a helicopter rescued three people in Heaps Canyon after flash flooding hit. North of Phoenix, a truck was swept away in a wash. The driver got out safely, Maricopa County sheriff’s officials said. The rocky, desert area typically gets less than 10 inches (25 centimeters) of rain annually with little vegetation to soak it up, making flash flooding a perpetual risk. The Bureau of Land Management in Arizona also reported significant flooding and damage to access roads in a national conservation area and a sand dunes recreation area in the southeastern part of the state. Back in Utah, the East Fork of the Virgin River near Zion raged with chocolate floodwater and a shipping container floated downstream. In the small town of Orderville, Utah, where flooding began Monday night, Sabrina Dubay was driving home when her partner called and told her to stay away. “The river came in and swept around the entirety of our house,” Dubay said. A camper, snowmobile trailer, and other items from Dubay’s yard were swept away by the river. Neighbors and friends arrived to dig a trench around the house as the water rose around their home. “It was coming in through our front doors,” she said. An unusually soggy September across the region set the stage: When the ground is saturated, rainfall has nowhere to go but run off. “Runoff is likely going to start much quicker and lead to those flooding impacts quicker,” Greulich said. By late Tuesday, rain had started in parts of the Oklahoma and Texas panhandles. Parts of Colorado, Kansas, Nebraska and Iowa were under flood watches, with flooding possible through at least Thursday. Baja California residents were ‘lucky’ Hurricane Polo pummeled Baja California Sur with powerful winds and rain as it made landfall. After Polo passed over the small fishing town of Puerto San Carlos on the Baja California peninsula, residents waded among downed trees through ankle-high water that flooded some homes. Seeing their roughened community largely intact brought relief to those who had prepared for the worst. Shopkeeper Elbia María Bachomo, 40, picked through furniture strewn through her home. She and her three children had gathered their clothes quickly and left for a shelter Monday as water began flooding into their home. Her husband was out on the water fishing for sardines when Polo hit. Bachomo said he was fortunate to escape alive. “I thought, ‘Oh no, what are we going to come back to? We will be left with nothing.’ But we were lucky,” she said. Hundreds of people were in shelters Tuesday in Baja California Sur, but they were expected to return to their homes. Meanwhile, the hurricane center reported Tropical Storm Rachel was moving parallel to Mexico’s coast Tuesday and was expected to become a hurricane soon. The storm was about 300 miles (482.8 kilometers) west-southwest of Lazaro Cardenos with maximum sustained winds of 70 mph (112.6 kph). It was moving northwest at 13 mph (20 kph). In the central Pacific Ocean, Hurricane Nolo was starting to slow Tuesday but still threatened dangerous conditions for parts of Papahanaumokuakea Marine National Monument, a marine conservation area. The storm moved northward after drenching parts of the Big Island over the weekend. Pacific storm activity has been above average this year. That is consistent with El Niño years.

articles.title: US actor Chad Lowe 'heartbroken' after death of daughter Fiona aged 13
articles.summary: Lowe and his wife Kim Painter announce the death of their daughter, who "was the light of our lives".
articles.body:
US actor Chad Lowe and his wife, producer Kim Painter, have said they are "deeply heartbroken" following the death of their "beloved" 13-year-old daughter Fiona.

"She was a loving young girl who was smart, creative and loved to dance," the family said in a statement to Page Six and People .

"She was adored by her sisters and she was deeply loved by her parents. In fact, she was the light of our lives.

"Her passing is devastating for our entire family and we ask for prayers and privacy at this time."

The statement concluded: "If you or someone you know is struggling with mental health, please reach out to the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline by calling or texting 988."

Chad Lowe, the brother of fellow actor Rob Lowe, won an Emmy Award in 1993 for TV show Life Goes On and has appeared in other programmes including Pretty Little Liars and Supergirl.

He and Painter are also parents to daughters Mabel, 17, and Nixie, 10.

articles.title: In 2005, North Carolina researchers put recycled nylon carpet fibres into asphalt; lab tests gave the mix 85% higher fracture energy, helping fight cracks
articles.summary: Discover how North Carolina researchers are innovating road repair by blending recycled carpet fibers into asphalt, improving fracture energy by 85% and providing a sustainable solution to road maintenance.
articles.body: Road surfaces can develop cracks and potholes as repeated traffic, temperature changes and moisture gradually wear down asphalt. Water seeps into every crack, heat softens the surface, traffic pounds it all day, and tiny splits gradually enlarge. Engineers have spent decades investigating how to strengthen asphalt without driving up expenses because repairs are expensive and seldom last.A 2005 North Carolina State University study tested recycled nylon carpet fibers in asphalt to examine whether they could improve resistance to fatigue cracking. Published in the Textile Research Journal, the study found that samples containing the optimal fiber combination had 85% higher fracture energy than asphalt without fibers, indicating improved resistance to fatigue cracking.The study suggests that recycled carpet fibers could improve asphalt's resistance to fatigue cracking. It was a laboratory finding, not a live road result, and the fibres were nylon, the kind used on the face of carpets. Still, the results pointed to a feasible means to reuse tough waste and extend the life of roadways.What lab tests revealedNylon is a common yarn in carpets, so the team used it as a proxy for recycled carpet fibre. They started with a single fibre pull-out test on 15 denier nylon strands, which indicates how tightly asphalt grabs a fibre. The critical embedded length came out at 9.2 millimetres. That is the point at which a fibre is gripped firmly enough to snap before slipping out of the mix.The researchers, armed with this amount, prepared samples of asphalt with fibres of two lengths, 6 and 12 millimetres, added at 0.25, 0.5 and 1% of the mix by volume. Then they conducted indirect tensile strength testing, a routine procedure that slices a cylinder of asphalt across its breadth. The best performing sample was 12-millimetre fibres at 1% by volume, with 85% more fracture energy than asphalt without fibres.Fracture energy is just the amount of work a material can do before it breaks. Asphalt is fragile in tension, and as vehicles repeatedly bend the surface for years, fatigue cracking occurs. Fibres behave like small bridges over a new crack and slow its growth. The researchers said the higher fracture energy indicated potential for improving asphalt fatigue life through recycled carpet fibers.Why carpet waste is a big dealCarpet can be difficult to recover because it is a layered product made from fibers, backing and other materials. Carpets and rugs generated 3.4 million tons of municipal solid waste in 2018, according to the US Environmental Protection Agency. That represented 1.2% of total MSW generation that year. The EPA’s table shows the scale of the waste stream behind that figure: in 2018, carpets and rugs generated 3.4 million tons of MSW, or 1.2% of the total, and only 310,000 tons were recycled. Most of the material was landfilled, underscoring why carpet recovery remains a persistent disposal problem.Some of it naturally belongs on roads. A highway requires huge quantities of material, and in the North Carolina tests, the fibres were 1 per cent or less of the mix by volume. A tiny dose, repeated over kilometres of road, could therefore take in a great deal of discarded carpet without changing how the road is laid. Roads that crack less also need fewer repairs, and every repair means more bitumen, more stone and more traffic held up while crews work.There’s a cost aspect, too. Waste fibres are cheaper than fibres produced for a specific task and a contractor might in theory obtain the same crack-combating advantage at a lower price. It is a reasonable question whether that saving survives collection, cleaning and shredding, and it is one reason why a good test result is only the first step.Earlier research had already tested waste fibersIn a 2004 study published in Resources, Conservation and Recycling, Bradley Putman and Serji Amirkhanian examined waste tire and carpet fibers in stone matrix asphalt, a rut-resistant mix used on heavily trafficked roadways. In such a mixture, adding fibres generally prevents the thick binder from draining off the stone, allowing waste fibres to perform the same function as manufactured ones. The authors noted that people commonly dump waste fibres in landfills and that using them would ease the load on those sites.More fibre is not necessarily better than less. Studies of various types of fibre show that resistance to cracking rises to an optimum level and then diminishes. The 2005 experiments used nylon carpet fibers, while a separate 2004 study had already examined waste carpet and tire fibers in stone matrix asphalt. Nor can a lab sample replicate years of traffic, heat and rain; thus, field trials on real roads remain the only honest test.The 2005 North Carolina study found 85% higher fracture energy at the best fiber setting. Later work on waste fibres in asphalt suggests the concept is viable. What’s missing is long-term proof on real roads. Until then, reclaimed carpet is a sensible, low-cost idea worth watching and not yet a ready-made fix.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: The US military says its withdrawal of troops from Iraq is complete
articles.summary: The US military announced on Wednesday that it has completed the withdrawal of its troops from Iraq, ending a 12-year mission to fight the Islamic State group.
articles.body: The US military announced on Wednesday that it has completed the withdrawal of its troops from Iraq, ending a 12-year mission to fight the Islamic State group. The last US troops left the last air base where they had been present in northern Iraq under an agreement between Baghdad and Washington. The move, which came in the midst of an ongoing war between the United States and Iran that has also sometimes spilled over into Iraq, was touted by Baghdad as a sign of the country’s increasing strength and sovereignty. The withdrawal was also celebrated by Iran-backed groups but raised concerns among some other other Iraqis, particularly in the Kurdish region. Pentagon spokesperson Sean Parnell said in a statement that US troops and equipment had completed an “orderly departure” from the air base in Irbil, in northern Iraq’s semi-autonomous Kurdish region. “This milestone reflects the success of a 12-year campaign that defeated ISIS as an organized military threat in Iraq and across the region,” he said. “It also marks a transition from a wartime coalition mission to an Iraqi-led security effort supported by a more normal bilateral security relationship.” Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi presided over the handover ceremony and described the US withdrawal as the beginning of a “a new phase, one defined by Iraq’s sovereignty, the strength of its institutions, the readiness of its forces, the unity of its decision-making, and balanced partnerships with its friends.” US troops invaded Iraq in 2003 to topple Saddam Hussein. They departed in 2011, but three years later, Iraqi authorities invited a smaller US-led mission to fight the Islamic State group, which had rampaged across Iraq, seizing large swaths of territory. With the extremist group reduced to scattered sleeper cells, Washington and Baghdad agreed in 2024 to wind the mission down. US troops pulled out of bases in most areas of Iraq last year but maintained a small presence of hundreds of troops in the semiautonomous northern Kurdish region. Bases there have regularly come under attack since the US and Israel launched their war against Iran on February 28. Iran-backed Iraqi militias also have coordinated with Yemen’s Houthi rebels to attack Saudi Arabia. The Iraqi government initially linked the September 30 deadline for US withdrawal to the disarmament of non-state armed groups by that date. While a handful of less-influential militias have agreed to turn over their weapons, powerful groups close to Iran rejected the prospect or set conditions for disarming that the government would be unlikely to meet. Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi has since walked back the deadline. He told The New York Times earlier this month that the deadline for militia disarmament has been pushed to June 2027. The effects of the US withdrawal may not be immediately visible, particularly since the US military presence had already been scaled down. But officials in Iraq’s Kurdish region have expressed anxiety about the departure and particularly about the removal of US air defense systems. The Kurdish regional government’s Peshmerga Ministry said the Kurdish region had faced more than 1,000 drone and ballistic-missile attacks during the recent US-Iran conflict. “The departure of the United States from the Kurdistan Region under these complex regional circumstances, without the provision of a defense system, is a matter of concern,” the statement said. Iran-allied groups in Iraq, meanwhile, have celebrated the US withdrawal. “The expulsion of the occupation forces, defeated, from the land of Iraq is the beginning of full sovereignty,” Abu Mujahid al-Assaf, a security official with the powerful Kataib Hezbollah militia, said in a statement. He added a warning to al-Zaidi and his government not to carry out American plans, threatening that “any government that does not work for the benefit of the people will be overthrown by all means.”

articles.title: Peter Murrell's legal aid withdrawn after embezzlement conviction
articles.summary: The former SNP chief executive had been receiving government-funded support since last year.
articles.body:
Former SNP chief executive Peter Murrell, who was jailed in June for embezzling more than £400,000 from the party, has had his legal aid withdrawn.

Murrell, the estranged husband of ex-First Minister Nicola Sturgeon, was sentenced to five years after using the funds to buy goods ranging from a luxury motorhome to toiletries.

He was granted legal aid - government-funded assistance typically given to people who cannot afford it - last year.

But The Scotsman reported that Murrell was informed his support would be withdrawn on 28 July.

The Scottish Legal Aid Board paid out £4,831 to fund legal counsel for Murrell.

That total could rise, as his lawyers could request payment for work carried out before the legal aid was withdrawn.

Peter Murrell jailed for more than five years for embezzling SNP funds

SNP write-off value of Murrell motorhome in party accounts

Legal aid is typically granted to people who would struggle to pay for legal help themselves, though in some cases they still need to make their own contribution.

A spokesperson for the Scottish Legal Aid Board confirmed that Murrell was "no longer in receipt of legal aid".

They added: "Legal aid and data protection legislation strictly limits what Slab can disclose about individual applications."

During Murrell's sentencing, the court was told that he had more than £600,000 across two pension accounts and would be able to pay back the sum embezzled, totalling £400,310.65.

The Herald reported last month that £4,831 of legal aid had been spent on Murrell's case. It is understood that sum has not changed.

A Scottish Legal Aid Board spokesperson told The Herald: "Legal representatives can send us bills during a case, or up to four months after it ends.

"We have not received any bills from the solicitors in this case yet, so we expect to make further payments."

The Scottish Legal Aid Board has not commented on why Murrell's support has been withdrawn.

Its website lists various reasons why it could drop legal aid - including a client providing false information, failing to disclose relevant information or conducting themselves "in an unreasonable way".

The board can also recover funds from recipients if their legal aid has been terminated.

Police Scotland began investigating the SNP's finances in 2021 after questions were asked about what had happened to £667,000 raised for a second independence referendum campaign.

Officers initially looking into those concerns ultimately uncovered Murrell's crimes.

They found the former chief executive had used charge cards, bank transfers and fake invoices to illicitly purchase items including jewellery, cosmetics, stationery, and games consoles.

Most notably, he bought a £124,500 motorhome in 2020.

Three years later, it was seized from his mother's driveway in Dunfermline with four miles on the clock.

articles.title: Here’s what’s happening at Paris Fashion Week
articles.summary: The biggest arena for the industry’s battle of ideas, is in full swing. Rihanna’s here, maniacal crowds are lining up outside shows to wave at their favorite stars and days of runway events lie ahead.
articles.body: Paris Fashion Week, the biggest arena for the industry’s battle of ideas, is in full swing. Rihanna’s here, maniacal crowds are lining up outside shows to screech and wave at their favorite stars and days of runway events big and small lie ahead. If Monday’s opening day was defined by a series of thinky shows by emerging ingenues including the creative duo behind Matières Fécales, Swedish one to watch Ellen Hodakova Larsson, and LVMH prize-winner Julie Kegels, Tuesday was when big houses like Dior and Saint Laurent ramped things up with their high octane productions and masterful collections. Cult brand Maison Margiela, the label behind the freaky looking tabi shoe, also staged its latest renegade runway show. Against a backdrop of wilting flowers that left a subtle funk in the air, designer Glenn Martens once again put forth ideas that challenged conventions of beautiful clothing. Models walked in toeless, knee-high boots in sculpted blazers and shirts that left the chest open and gaping, and floral prints clashed with the set behind them. There’s a lot going on in the French capital this week. Follow our coverage as we zoom in and out on the little delights and big moments that grabbed our attention. This story is ongoing and will be updated. A gilded goodbye at Saint Laurent? The Saint Laurent show, staged under the dramatic glow of the Eiffel Tower, has long been a buzzy tentpole of Paris Fashion Week. But on Tuesday the energy of the event revved up further amid speculation that the show would be creative director Anthony Vaccarello’s last after ten years at the house. The almost all-gold collection certainly suggested a milestone moment. Alchemic looks rendered in many shades and textures of gold looked back at archetypes from Yves Saint Laurent’s heyday — Safari-style jackets, trenches and wrap skirts — while more modern silhouettes such as Vaccarello’s bouncy blouson jackets reminded those watching of his impact at the house. The runway event ended with a performance by Charlotte Gainsbourg and a standing ovation for Vaccarello who wrote in the show notes, “A light shines all the more brightly because we know it cannot be held. What passes sometimes leaves more light than what remain.” Jonathan Anderson’s take on romance at Dior Imagine a rich young thing throwing her fanciful clothes over the door of a bedroom armoire before falling into bed, makeup on, at the end of a day. These were the pieces that Dior’s Jonathan Anderson sent down the runway in the Jardin des Tuileries on Tuesday afternoon. Once again guests were seated around a circular pond under scorching heat, the misty water and breezy flounce of the clothes offering little physical respite from the realities of our surroundings, but managing for a moment to export us away mentally. Skirts, tops and what looked like earrings made of layers of circle-cut chiffon, and light as air sheer jacketing suggested Anderson was looking to define his version of romance, a mood the French house has long-conjured during its history. While his love story felt young and full of hope, it wasn’t naive — any prissyness was broken up with sharper elements like a series of python-effect metallic trousers and modern styling that left shirts loose and untucked and allowed checks and patterns to clash. Power to the people at Matières Fécales In a challenging economy brands aren’t much for taking big risks or causing upset, so Matières Fécales bold, statement-making show that saw models stomp down the runway with mannequins representing the wealthy elite slumped over their backs had no trouble gaining traction online, thanks also to the hype-inducing appearance of Rihanna who sat front row. Steven Raj Bhaskaran, who is partnered in life and work with Hannah Rose Dalton, wrote in show notes that the collection was focussing on empowering “those most vulnerable in the Ninety Nine Per Cent.”

articles.title: Photos: A journalist is crowned king in Uganda
articles.summary: The death of King Oyo Nyimba in August triggered widespread grief and a succession dispute in Uganda’s Tooro Kingdom.
articles.body:
A journalist has been crowned king of Uganda’s Tooro Kingdom, a traditional monarchy plunged into grief and a succession dispute following the death of its “boy king” last month.

Prince Edward Rukidi Nyabongo, long employed as a broadcaster and editor with the state-run Uganda Broadcasting Corporation, took his regnal name after performing night-time rituals before being ushered into the palace.

He was formally unveiled to his subjects on Tuesday in Fort Portal, a town in western Uganda near the border with the Democratic Republic of the Congo.

Uganda’s traditional kingdoms were abolished in the 1960s by a republican president seeking to unify the newly independent country, but were restored in 1993.

While cultural monarchs hold no constitutional powers and are barred from partisan politics, they retain significant influence as custodians of tradition and identity.

Speaking at the ceremony, President Yoweri Museveni urged traditional leaders to promote local languages.

Nyabongo, in a short address, promised to be a unifying figure and told the New Vision newspaper that “heritage must be matched by discipline and hard work”, describing royal descent as a duty rather than an entitlement.

Nyabongo was not high in the line of succession. Elders of the ruling Babiito clan selected him from a pool of eligible princes after King Oyo Nyimba Kabamba Iguru Rukidi IV died of cancer in August at the age of 34, reportedly without a publicly acknowledged heir.

The queen mother, Best Kemigisa, has challenged the decision, claiming Oyo left a young son whose identity will be revealed “at the right time”. The prospect of a “Baby Oyo” has stirred supporters on social media and raised questions over the legitimacy of Nyabongo’s coronation.

articles.title: Singapore launches matchmaking service for government workers
articles.summary: The launch of FirstDate comes as the ageing nation wrestles with a record-low fertility rate.
articles.body:
Singapore has rolled out a matchmaking service for its government workers, an initiative that comes as the country wrestles with a record-low fertility rate.

FirstDate, which launched this week for those aged 21 to 35, boasts "a different approach to dating", where it uses a Nobel-winning algorithm to match participants to one date at a time. "Swipe fatigue ends here," its website reads.

Participants sign in using the national digital identity system and answer a survey about their interests, habits and values.

FirstDate's launch drew mixed responses among Singaporeans, with some describing it as "dystopian" and others saying they would be keen to give it a shot.

On its website, FirstDate highlights the Gale-Shapley Stable Marriage algorithm which powers the programme.

The mathematical framework pairs two equally sized groups of people based on their preferences.

The late mathematician Lloyd Shapley was awarded the 2012 Nobel memorial prize in economic sciences for discovering the algorithm, which has been used in public school admissions, medical residency matching, and dating apps, among other things.

"At the end of the day, I think the experience of meeting someone through an application doesn't change much across the [different types of] applications," Elizabeth, a 29-year-old who works in Singapore's defence ministry and is keen on trying FirstDate out told the BBC.

"But it is nice to know that the likelihood of being scammed is much lower. We're all public servants looking for a partner, right?"

But some social media users say the initiative, which is currently in its pilot phase, discriminates against those not working in government.

Others criticised the age limit. "They are only doing this to raise the total fertility rate. They don't actually [care] about whether we find a partner otherwise.

"Since there are higher risks involved in having kids at 35 and older, the government just writes [the older singles] off," wrote another Reddit user.

It is not clear if the pilot programme will be available to the wider public in future. The BBC has reached out to GovTech, the statutory board behind the pilot, for comment.

The pilot launch comes as Singapore's birth rate has slumped to historic lows. For the first time in the past 60 years, fewer than 30,000 babies were born in 2025.

The number of deaths meanwhile have been rising steadily in the greying nation, hitting about 26,500 in 2025.

In August, Prime Minister Lawrence Wong announced a series of new measures to better support families and to encourage couples to have children, including almost S$70,000 ($54,000; £41,000) in financial support for every child by the time they turn 17.

FirstDate is not the first time the citystate is trying to play Cupid to its citizens.

In 1984, it set up the Social Development Unit (SDU) tasked with organising social events to encourage graduate singles to mingle.

Its exclusive target audience of university graduates was criticised as being elitist, but authorities justified the approach saying non-graduates did not seem to have difficulty finding partners. The SDU was eventually phased out.

The next year, the government set up another agency to promote marriages among non-graduates.

The idea of a government-run dating service is not unique to Singapore. In September 2024, Tokyo's metropolitan government launched an AI-powered dating app in an effort to combat the country's declining birth rate.

The app, which is open to single residents in the city, resulted in 265 couples getting married, according to government data released in July this year.

Additional reporting by Osmond Chia in Singapore
